Mr. Shah Hossein, Advocate ------ for the Petitioners. 
Mr. Yusuf Hossain Humayun, Advocate ------ for the Opposite Party nos. 1 and 2.
parties:
Nazmul Alam and others
Vs.
President, Governing Body, Mozahar Uddin Biswas Degree College, Kalapara, Patuakiiali and others
full_judgment:
A.N.M. Bashir Ullah, J: This Rule, on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the Code) at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 25.04.2012 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Patuakhali in Miscellaneous Appeal no. 15 of 2011 setting aside the judgment and order dated 08.05.2011 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Kalapara, Patuakhali in Title Suit no. 159 of 2010 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted title Suit no. 159 of 2010 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kalapara, Patuakhali for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from appointing any lecturer/teacher in the department of History and Accounting in the Mozahar Uddin Biswas Degree College, Kalapara, Patuakhali (in short the College) on the strength of an advertisement published in the Daily Janakantha dated 29.10.2010 and also for mandatory injunction directing the defendants to take proper step for enlisting the names of the plaintiffs in the Monthly Payment Order (in short, the MPO). 

 3. The suit was followed by a prayer for permanent injunction under Order 39 rule 1 of the Code averring inter-alia that the College authority in pursuant of an advertisement selected the plaintiff nos. 1 and 2 as lecturer for the department of History and plaintiff no. 3 for the department of Accounting and they were appointed by the authority of the College on 30.08.2006 and accordingly they joined in their respective post on 31.08.2006 and from then they have been discharging their duties to the satisfaction of all concerns. 

 4. During the immediate past caretaker government, the enlistment of the MPO's and the approval of the academic institutions were suspended for various reasons. The plaintiffs have not been enlisted in the MPO's list till now. It was the incumbent duty of the defendant nos. 1 and 2 to take arrangement so that the plaintiffs can be enlisted in the MPO's list but they did not take any proper step to that effect. Rather, the defendant nos. 1 and 2 surprisingly published an advertisement in the Daily Janakantha dated 29.10.2010 for the appointment of lecturers in the department of History and Accounting, which is illegal and unwarranted. 

 5. In the department of History, the total strength of students did not justify more then two lecturers and as against the said two posts plaintiff nos. 1 and 2 have been serving there and in the department of Accounting there is a total strength of two lecturers and as against the said two posts the plaintiff no. 3 and one Delwar Hossain have been serving. So, there appears no vacant post in the departments of History and Accounting. But even then the defendants by passing and ignoring the service and appointment of the plaintiffs made those advertisement in the daily newspaper and under the said compelling circumstances, the plaintiffs have been constrained to file the suit as well as the prayer for temporary injunction, so, that the College authority cannot appoint lecturers in the department of History and Accounting on the strength of the advertisement dated 29.10.2010. 

 6. On receipt of the prayer for temporary injunction, the trial Court by its order dated 23.11.2010 issued an order of show cause against the defendants. The defendant no. 2 appearing in the suit on 02.01.2011 filed written objection against the prayer for temporary injunction. In the written objection it was asserted among others that the prayer for temporary injunction is not maintainable in its present form, the plaintiffs have filed the suit as well as the prayer for permanent injunction to cause harm in the smooth functioning of the College. The case of the defendant no. 2, in short, is that 9 teachers were appointed by the College authority including the plaintiffs on 30.08.2006 and the some was approved by the governing body of the College on 10.09.2006. The plaintiffs had no any registration for such appointment but relying on their assurance that at their own instance they will be enlisted in the MPO's list they were appointed in their deserving post of the College. But ultimately the plaintiffs have been baffled to be enlisted in the MPO's list and the higher authority by their letter dated 14.02.2007 informed the College that since the plaintiffs have no any registration and index number they are not eligible to be enlisted in the MPO's list. Under the above facts and circumstances their appointment has been cancelled automatically. 

 7. The further case of the defendant is that one Parimal Kumar Dutta, Assistant Professor, department of History has been retired from the service. So, in order to appoint lecturer in the said vacant post and also in some other vacant posts an advertisement was published on behalf of the College on 29.10.2010 in the Daily Janakantha. The plaintiff no. 1 had been serving at Dashmina Alipur College, the plaintiff no. 2 at Dhankali College and plaintiff no. 3 at Mohipur Muktijoddah Memorial College before joining in the Mozahar Uddin Biswas Degree College. It is the mandatory provisions that in transferring service from one College to another College every lecturer/teacher must have the registration and index number. But they had no such registration and index number. So, the plaintiffs cannot claim anything in their favour to work or serve as lecturer in a College. So, the prayer for permanent injunction is liable to be rejected. 

 8. After filing of the above written objection in the trail Court, the suit was fixed on 08.05.2011 for hearing of the temporary injunction matter. But on that day, the matter was heard in the absence of the contesting defendants and the trial Court passed an order of temporary injunction in favour of the plaintiffs and as against that order the defendant no. 2 preferred Miscellaneous appeal being no. 5 of 2011 in the Court of District Judge, Patuakhali which has been ultimately heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Patuakhali who by his impugned judgment dated 25.04.2012 allowed the appeal setting aside those of the judgment and order of temporary injunction dated 08.05.2011. The plaintiff-petitioners being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and order moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. The rule is resisted by the opposite party nos. 1 and 2. 

 9. Mr. Shah Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners supports the Rule. He submits that the trial Court considering the prima facie and arguable case in favour of the plaintiffs granted temporary injunction restraining the defendants from making appointment in the post of lecturers in the department of History and Accounting in place of the plaintiffs. But the appellate Court below being misconceived of the facts came to a wrong conclusion that the College authority is going to appoint lecturers as against the vacant post in the department of History and Accounting of the College. The College authority in fact has been trying to appoint the new lecturers in the place of the plaintiffs. So, the appellate Court below should have affirmed the judgment of the trial Court. But on some wrong and erroneous view set aside the judgment of the trial Court. So, the Rule should be made absolute restoring the judgment and order of the trial Court. 

 10. On the other hand, Mr. Yusuf Hossain Humayun, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party nos. 1 and 2 opposing the Rule very strongly submits that the plaintiffs were appointed in the College on 30.08.2006 and they joined in their respective post on 31.08.2006. All of them had come in the College from other Colleges and at the relevant time they could not show their registration and index number which are the prerequisites for the appointment in the post of lecturer of a College but they assured the College authority both orally and in black and white that they will procure the same. But within a long gap of 4-5 years they could not procure the same. So, they cannot claim their continuation in their respective post. 

 12. He also submits that the plaintiffs could not obtain the registration as required under sections 10 of Besarkari Sikkhok Nibondhan-O-Prottayan Ain, 2005 (in short, the Ain, 2005). So, the plaintiffs have no any prima-facie and arguable case in their favour for granting injunction and the appellate Court below rightly considering the said facts and circumstances of the case rejected the prayer for temporary injunction. So, the said impugned judgment and order of the appellate Court below do not call for any interference from this Court. 

 13. He also submits that all the plaintiffs were reportedly appointed in some other Colleges before their appointment in the Mozahar Uddin Biswas Degree College. But their previous appointment were also illegal. As such they are not entitled to get the benefit of proviso of subsection (2) of section 10 of the Ain, 2005. 

 15. From the materials on record it appears that the plaintiffs sought injunction in the trial Court filing a prayer for temporary injunction on 23.11.2010 and on that day an order of show cause was passed upon the defendants and after a reasonable gap the injunction mater was heard by the trial Court exparte on 08.05.2011 and an order of temporary injunction was passed against the defendants. 

 18. The learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-opposite parties submits that before granting temporary injunction one Mr. Mustafizur Rahman and Abu Saley have been appointed in the department of History and Accounting on 28.03.2011 which is much earlier than that of the date of granting injunction. There appears some paper as to the appointment of Mustafizur Rahman and Abu Saley in the record. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioners submits that this important fact has not been stated in the written objection. The written objection was filed on 02.01.2011, so there was a little scope for the defendants to articulate this fact in the written objection. 

 19. The bone contention of the submissions of the plaintiffs is that the College authority took initiative to appoint lecturers in the department of History and Accounting in their place. In this connection, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties categorically submits that Mr. Parimal Chandra Dutta, Assistant Professor, department of History has been retired from the College on 31.03.2008 and Mr. Bupendranath Biswas Assistant Professor, department of Accounting has been retired from the service on 07.05.2009 and as against the said vacant posts the advertisement was published in the daily Janakantha and by this time pursuant to the said advertisement 2(two) lecturers in the department of History and. Accounting in their place have already been appointed on 28.03.2011. 

 21. In this hearing some allegations were made by the opposite party nos. 1 and 2 as to the eligibility of the plaintiffs for their appointment as lecturers in the private College. In my consideration this sorts of allegation can be scrutinized at the time trial. But the sub-section (2) of section 10 of the Ain, 2005 runs as follows: 

 22. It is submitted by both the parties that the Ain, 2005 came into force on 20.03.2005. The plaintiffs were appointed in the College on 30.08.2006. Under the above facts and circumstances since they were appointed in the Mozahar Uddin Biswas Degree College in the year 2006 so, they have the privilege to avail the benefit of proviso of sub-section (2) of section 10 of the Ain, 2005. But in this regard, the definite case of the opposite party nos. 1 and 2 that at the time of their first appointment in the other Colleges either they had no minimum requirements for appointment or the institution itself in which they were appointed was not legal. As, this is a pure question of fact, the same cannot be determined without a trial. It is admitted that the plaintiffs have no any registration and index number which are visualized from a written instrument signed by them at the eve of their appointment in the College. Since the deserving vacant post has already been filled up by the College authority, so, the injunction petition is not maintainable at all in the eye of law. Accordingly, I find no merit in the Rule.
